memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "His father Isaac answered him, 'Your dwelling will be away from the earth's richness, away from the dew of heaven above. You will live by the sword and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will throw his yoke from off your neck.'" - Gen 27:39-40 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Isaac speaks over Esau a future far harder than Jacob's — a life away from the richest land, lived by the sword, and for a time under his brother. It was not the blessing Esau longed for. Yet even here there is a glimmer: "when you grow restless, you will throw his yoke from off your neck." His future held struggle, but not endless bondage.

This is a hard passage, and we should be honest about it. Esau's path would be difficult, shaped in part by the choices already made. Life is not always fair, and some of us begin from harder places than others. Esau did not receive what his brother received.

But notice: God did not abandon Esau. He went on to become the father of the Edomites, a real nation with its own place in history. Even the son who missed the covenant blessing was not forgotten by God. The Lord's care extends beyond the boundaries of promise.

If you feel your road is harder than others', take heart. God sees you, and He is not absent from difficult paths. Your circumstances do not define your worth in His eyes, and His grace can meet you even where the road is steep. No life lies outside the reach of His compassion.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I trust that God sees me even when my road is hard?
2. Where do I compare my "portion" to others' and lose heart?
3. How can I trust God's care beyond my circumstances?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, when my road feels harder than others', help me to trust that You see me and have not forgotten me. Meet me with Your grace on the steep paths. Amen.
